question: Certain glucose transporters that are expressed predominantly on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes are unique compared to those transporters found on other cell types within the body. Without directly affecting glucose transport in other cell types, which of the following would be most likely to selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes?

options.ope: It is physiologically impossible to selectively increase glucose uptake in specific cells

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Increased levels of circulating insulin -> Activation of insulin receptors on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Increased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane -> Enhanced glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Selective increase in glucose uptake in these cells -> 95%

CHAIN: Decreased levels of circulating insulin -> Reduced activation of insulin receptors on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Decreased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane -> Impaired glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> 90%
enhanced_information: Increased levels of circulating insulin would most likely selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes. This is supported by the activation of insulin receptors on these cells, leading to increased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane, enhancing glucose uptake selectively in these cells.
analysis: Increased levels of circulating insulin would most likely selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes by activating insulin receptors and promoting GLUT4 translocation to the cell membrane. This is a well-established physiological mechanism.
